summary: Midstream proxy pipelining inserts keepalive wedge and stream closes without terminal marker, truncating final code block
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that SSE streams to their web client terminate prematurely after a midstream proxy pipelining interaction. The last markdown code block (delimited by triple backticks) is absent from the final stream; instead the client receives a keepalive line injected by an internal edge proxy and then an apparent stream closure with no 'event: end' or explicit terminal JSON marker.

Impact:
- Acme Analytics users see truncated outputs in 12% of long-form streaming responses for conversations > 4k tokens.
- Final code blocks used to deliver runnable examples are missing, causing product failures for their code-execution pipeline.
- Customer is enterprise tier with uptime SLA; requires mitigation and a permanent fix.

Environment:
- traffic path: client -> corp-edge-proxy (customer-managed) -> Redwood edge cluster -> api-gateway -> serving-runtime
- region: prod-us-east (us-east-1)
- affected models: redwood-v1-small, open-lite-2.1b
- observed since 2026-03-09 18:20 UTC after a change to proxy HTTP/2 pipelining and keepalive heuristics

Steps to reproduce (as reported):
1. Start a streaming SSE request from the Acme web client with a prompt that yields a final markdown code block and ~5k token output.
2. Midway through the response, trigger a short-lived upstream idle probe from the corporate edge (simulate with their proxy test harness).
3. Observe received SSE frames in browser network tab and the final assembled JSON in the client SDK.

Observed behavior:
- An ':",heartbeat
' style keepalive line is injected in the middle of a token chunk (boundary inside multi-byte UTF-8 chunk).
- The server-side stream continues briefly then the connection is closed by the proxy with 502/connection reset-to-client semantics.
- Client-side SDK reopens and attempts resume but the resume offset gets anchored to the injected keepalive frame offset rather than the last valid token index.
- As a result, the final code block is never emitted and some middle paragraphs duplicate upon resume.

Expected behavior:
- Keepalive frames should not be treated as resume anchors; the server should emit an explicit terminal marker (event: end / final chunk) before any upstream connection termination, or the client resume protocol should prefer last-application-token offset.

Logs & evidence attached (links):
- Edge request trace: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/edge/trace-20260309-1a2b3c
- Serving runtime tail logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/serving/runtime/2026-03-09/edge-serve-tail.log (snippet lines 412-438 show keepalive injection)
- Client HAR from Acme (redacted) attached to ticket.

Initial hypotheses:
- The customer-managed proxy performs HTTP/2 pipelining/merge that injects zero-length keepalive frames which the resume algorithm incorrectly indexes as stream offsets.
- The serving runtime's resume token map does not discriminate control/keepalive frames from application frames when forming resume cursors.

Immediate customer-facing workaround suggested:
1) Ask Acme to temporarily disable HTTP/2 pipelining / merge on their corp-edge-proxy for traffic to Redwood endpoints, or to increase idle probe interval.
2) Use a non-streaming fallback for critical code-generation requests until fix is deployed.

Follow-up/next steps for internal team:
- SRE to reproduce with a local proxy harness and confirm offset mapping behavior (assigned).
- Engineering to add a heuristic to ignore keepalive/control frames when generating resume offsets and to ensure terminal markers are flushed on connection anomalies.
- QA to add regression test covering mid-chunk keepalive injection during resume.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Pinging SRE and Edge teams. Customer reports consistent reproducible failure when they enable HTTP/2 pipelining. Attached HAR and logs. Marked P1 due to enterprise SLA.

2026-03-10 10:03 - SRE (Marta Liu): Reproduced locally with 'h2-proxy' harness. Observed injected "\\n:heartbeat\\n" lines arriving mid-chunk. Current resume implementation indexes stream by raw byte offset; confirmed regression when control frames are present.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Edge eng (Diego Ramirez): Added instrumentation to tag control frames in the edge decode path. Proposed patch to filter control frames when building resume cursors: PR https://github.com/redwood/realtime-proxy/pull/289. Will run canary after patch.

2026-03-11 08:45 - Support (Aisha Patel): Customer applied the temporary workaround (disabled pipelining) and confirmed immediate improvement — missing codeblock no longer observed in sampled requests during 8h window.

2026-03-12 16:55 - Diego Ramirez (Edge eng): Canary rollout of PR 289 succeeded in us-east-edge-canary (10% traffic). Observed 0 occurrences of truncated codeblock in canary logs for 24h. Preparing full rollout and postmortem entry.

2026-03-12 17:05 - Support (Aisha Patel): Notifying Acme about planned full rollout and recommending re-enable pipelining after 24h of stable canary metrics. Will keep ticket open until full deploy and customer sign-off.
resolution: Mitigated: edge proxy patch (PR 289) introduced filtering of keepalive/control frames from resume cursor computation and ensured explicit terminal marker flush on edge connection anomalies. Customer temporary workaround validated. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC.
